case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed an award of permanent custody to grandparents in a dependency case, holding that KRS 620.027 confers standing on grandparents with whom the child is actually residing in a stable relationship, independent of the de facto custodian requirements of KRS 403.270.
key_cases.relevance: This is the controlling Kentucky decision on KRS 620.027 grandparent standing to obtain permanent custody as a permanency outcome.
key_cases.quote: Once the family court makes a finding of a stable relationship between grandparent(s) and child, the court is to utilize KRS Chapter 403 to determine custodial arrangements.

key_cases.holding: The court held that a permanent custody award may be entered within a KRS Chapter 620 dependency action if the proper procedures are followed, but reversed because the family court failed to make sufficient findings on the KRS 403.270 best-interest factors and did not account for the mother's progress on her case plan.
key_cases.relevance: It is the Kentucky authority on converting a dependency case into a permanent third-party custody disposition.
key_cases.quote: such a hearing and an award of custody are not precluded by the structure of KRS Chapter 620, so long as the proper procedures are followed

key_cases.holding: The Court held that second cousins denied any consideration for relative placement, in derogation of the Cabinet's own standards, had a sufficient legal interest to intervene as of right in the foster parents' adoption proceeding; it vacated the adoption and ordered the Cabinet to evaluate the relatives.
key_cases.relevance: It establishes that relatives denied consideration may intervene to seek permanency for the child themselves.
key_cases.quote: Although the statute and regulations do not mandate that the Cabinet choose a relative placement over other options, they at the very least, require that the Cabinet consider relatives

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed the trial court's jurisdiction and reinstated its finding that the birth parents' adoption consents were not knowingly given, but held that the prospective adoptive parents had standing to seek custody and that the birth parents had waived their superior right to custody, so on remand custody must be decided on the child's best interest.
key_cases.relevance: It is the Kentucky Supreme Court's framework for a nonparent's standing to seek custody and for the waiver exception that permits a permanent third-party custody award decided on the child's best interest rather than on parental unfitness.
key_cases.quote: Like the final order in a TPR proceeding, a valid adoption judgment terminates the parental rights of the birth parent.

key_cases.holding: The court held that a permanent-custody order entered in a KRS Chapter 620 dependency action is a 'custody decree' subject to the modification restrictions of KRS 403.340 only if it was actually based on the best-interest standards of KRS 403.270(2); because the order here rested solely on a social worker's unsworn statement with no evidence taken, it was not, and the court vacated and remanded for a full custody hearing.
key_cases.relevance: It is the authority N.L. v. W.F. relies on for converting a dependency case into a permanent third-party custody disposition, and it specifies what a permanency order must contain to become a durable custody decree.
key_cases.quote: for a custody order to be a "custody decree," within the meaning of KRS Chapter 403, it must be based on the standards set out in KRS 403.270(2)
